D1.label: def:clipping
D1.name: Clipping
D1.raw_latex:
For any $M>0$ and $t\in\R$, we define the clipped version $\bar{t}$ of $t$ as
\[\bar{t} = \begin{cases} -M,& \mbox{if } t < -M \\ t, & \mbox{if } t \in [-M,M] \\ M, & \mbox{if } t > M. \end{cases}\] Similarly, the clipped version $\bar{f}$ of a function $f : \X\rightarrow \R$ is defined as
\[\forall x\in\X,\quad \bar{f}(x) = \overline{f(x)} = \begin{cases} -M,& \mbox{if } f(x) < -M \\ f(x), & \mbox{if } f(x) \in [-M,M] \\ M, & \mbox{if } f(x) > M. \end{cases}\] and $\bar{\F}$ denotes the clipped function class $\{\bar{f} : f \in \F\}$.
D1.clean_text: For any M > 0 and t in R, we define the clipped version t of t as t if t is in [-M, M], -M if t is less than -M, and M if t is greater than M. Similarly, the clipped version f of a function f from X to R is defined as f(x) if f(x) is in [-M, M], -M if f(x) is less than -M, and M if f(x) is greater than M. The clipped function class F is the set of all clipped functions of functions in F.
